scope: AI-002 sequential primary-to-backup routing, total deadline and template reserve, infrastructure and quality breakers with Redis CAS/loss behavior, live PublishGuard recheck, and low-cardinality normalized usage/cost telemetry

assertions: primary timeout advances once to backup with the same frozen plan, prepared input and route fingerprint, without racing or joining candidate fields
an OPEN primary route is skipped immediately and the independent backup route remains eligible
Safety and budget admission stop before breaker or provider access, and unreadable breaker state returns only CONTROLLED_TEMPLATE_REQUIRED
a fresh live guard after provider completion rejects stale, Safety, deletion or existing-result publication
replayed UNKNOWN attempt state advances to backup without adding a second infrastructure breaker sample
all route cases use synthetic immutable inputs and provider outcomes with no external provider, credential, user identity or real content
primary timeout produces exactly one backup candidate using the unchanged plan and prepared input
OPEN primary breaker state causes no primary dispatch and does not wait for cooldown before backup
five consecutive infrastructure failures OPEN the route with bounded 60/120/240/480/900 second cooldown policy
the bounded twenty-sample infrastructure window enforces the ten-sample minimum and fifty-percent threshold after either a failure or success
HALF_OPEN permits at most two claims and needs two successes to close while a probe failure reopens
auth and quality blocks remain until the exact route fingerprint changes
quality and neutral outcomes do not enter or reset the infrastructure denominator, and malformed persisted snapshots fail closed

T-AI002-BREAKER-AI-EVAL-001.selector: G12-B01 through G12-B05 deterministic breaker cases
assertions: each accepted S-12 breaker threshold is asserted against a deterministic synthetic outcome timeline
quality failures are counted only in the quality response window and never dilute the infrastructure denominator
auth and quality recovery requires a new immutable route fingerprint rather than elapsed time

T-AI002-BREAKER-REDIS-001.selector: AI-002 real Redis breaker CAS and loss fail closed
assertions: the Redis 8 adapter accepts exactly one of two concurrent missing-revision compare-and-set writes
a stale in-flight outcome with the same numeric revision but an old route fingerprint cannot overwrite a new route revision
the stored immutable breaker snapshot reads back exactly through the strict parser
stopping Redis makes breaker load return only the stable GATEWAY_BREAKER_STORE_UNAVAILABLE error
when remaining total time is below route deadline plus template reserve, no attempt is reserved and no provider is called
the caller receives the stable DEADLINE_RESERVE_REQUIRED fallback reason without extending the hard deadline
the fixed Daily eight-second timeline preserves at least one second for local validation and template work
the deterministic case uses only a synthetic clock and provider adapter and does not call a real provider

T-AI002-LATE-MODULE-001.selector: G12-L05 discards a provider response when the hard generation window closes
assertions: a complete provider response arriving at the hard deadline is not returned as a candidate
the attempt records LATE_RESPONSE_DISCARDED with OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and the caller can only enter a later bounded path
the fixed synthetic clock crosses the exact Daily generation deadline after the provider response
the late candidate body never enters the returned Gateway outcome or attempt metadata
known normalized input/output units and billed cost record their actual non-negative values
unknown usage and cost increment explicit unknown counters and are never coerced to zero
provider and model use closed role/revision buckets while route version, attempt identifiers, Prompt and content never become metric labels
breaker skips and final no-result routing decisions are separate low-cardinality signals
